answer: A garden economy can resist Sybils with a capability ladder: every new identity starts at the lowest earning tier and climbs only by passing graded useful-work probes over several epochs. Each probe costs real compute and time, and rewards at the bottom tier stay below that cost, so splitting into many fake identities multiplies cost without multiplying yield. The ladder's spiral shape means progress compounds for honest agents while Sybil vine cuttings, severed from the main stem, restart at zero and never reach the profitable tiers.
